title: fix(config): derive endpoint/webchat/static URLs for NiCE CXone hosts

findings.claim: The bug (host regex failing on cognigy-api-au1.nicecxone.com) no longer exists on main — fixed by merged PR #12 / commit 31ac010 (deriveHostBaseUrl with /(^|-)api-/); this PR's live diff is a redundant rename plus regression tests.
findings.evidence: First half CONFIRMED: git log shows 31ac010 'fix(config): derive endpoint/webchat/static URLs for prefixed tenant … (#12)' merged 2026-08-18, and current src/config.ts:67-78 has deriveHostBaseUrl with url.hostname.replace(/(^|-)api-/, ...), which handles cognigy-api-au1.nicecxone.com. Second half OVERSTATED: gh pr diff 1 (rebased, updatedAt 2026-08-25) is NOT purely rename+tests — it also fixes a real live bug on main: deriveHostBaseUrl returns `${url.protocol}//${url.hostname}` (src/config.ts:71), which DROPS an explicit port (api-trial.cognigy.ai:8443 → endpoint-trial.cognigy.ai, no port). The PR's new deriveSiblingBaseUrl preserves `url.port` and adds three port-preservation tests. It also adds a stderr warning when no 'api-' label exists, and rewrites the parse-failure fallback.

findings.claim: PR description is stale: claims a live 'silent misrouting bug' that no longer reproduces.
findings.evidence: gh pr view 1 body says src/config.ts currently 'matched the API hostname with /^api-(.+)$/' and 'Replaced the three near-identical derivations with a shared deriveSiblingBaseUrl()'. Neither is true of the merge base: main's src/config.ts:67-78 already has the shared deriveHostBaseUrl with the fixed /(^|-)api-/ regex since 31ac010 (#12, merged Aug 18; PR #1 created Jul 31). The CXone misrouting no longer reproduces on main — the diff itself shows the base file already containing the fix. The body also omits the port-preservation fix the diff actually delivers.

findings.claim: Prior verdict: merge with changes (rewrite description as tests+refactor).
findings.evidence: Direction confirmed — merge-with-changes is right and the description must be rewritten. But characterizing it as 'tests+refactor' undersells the port-drop fix (a genuine behavior fix vs main, src/config.ts:71) and misses that the PR's new parse-failure fallback (`apiBaseUrl.replace(/\/(.*-)?api-/, ...)`) regresses 31ac010's deliberate host-scoping: for a scheme-less unparseable input like 'api-dev.cognigy.ai/notes-api-v2', main returns it unchanged (fallback requires ^[a-z]+:// ), while the PR rewrites the PATH segment to '/notes-endpoint-v2'. Contrived edge, but it undoes an explicit prior fix ('scopes the non-URL fallback to the host portion only' — 31ac010 second commit message).

newFindings: Port-preservation is a real live fix the prior review missed: main's deriveHostBaseUrl (src/config.ts:71) returns protocol//hostname and silently drops an explicit port (e.g. :8443), so derived endpoint/webchat/static URLs lose the port; PR #1 fixes and tests this. The PR is therefore not fully redundant.

The PR's rewritten parse-failure fallback `apiBaseUrl.replace(/\/(.*-)?api-/, ...)` is no longer host-scoped, reintroducing the path-rewrite hazard that 31ac010's second commit deliberately removed (a scheme-less input with 'x-api-' in its path gets its path rewritten). Should be restored to a host-scoped replace.
The new no-'api-'-label warning uses console.error — safe for a stdio MCP server (stderr), but it fires three times per boot (endpoint, webchat, static) for the same host; cosmetic only.

usage.vibeExperience: Per migration-docs/arsalan-diff-comparison.md:162-174 ('Shared bug — mirror-image, both repos'): the team runs cognigy-vibe against NiCE CXone tenants only. They point it at https://cognigy-api-{region}.nicecxone.com and its api.py derives endpoint_base_url by replacing 'cognigy-api-' → 'cognigy-endpoint-' (throwing if the base isn't a CXone host), so posting test messages to an agent and getting webchat links 'just works' on CXone. The official plugin was cognigy.ai-only and failed silently on CXone hosts — the worse failure mode. This PR (and the already-merged #12) recreates that CXone experience, generalized to any '-api-' label.
usage.howToUseHere: 1) Configure credentials with the CXone API host: run `npx @cognigy/plugin-engine@latest cognigy-setup` and enter base URL `https://cognigy-api-au1.nicecxone.com` + your API key — or export COGNIGY_API_BASE_URL=https://cognigy-api-au1.nicecxone.com and COGNIGY_API_KEY=... before launching Claude Code. 2) In a live session the derived hosts are then used automatically by: `talk_to_agent { aiAgentId, message }` (handleTalkToAgent, handlers.ts:2068 — posts the test message to https://cognigy-endpoint-au1.nicecxone.com/<URLToken>); `create_ai_agent { name }` (returns endpointUrl on the cognigy-endpoint- host, handlers.ts:1600); `manage_webchat` (returns https://cognigy-webchat-au1.nicecxone.com/v3/<URLToken>, handlers.ts:4249); `manage_voice_gateway` / `audit_voice_agent` (webrtc link on https://cognigy-static-au1.nicecxone.com/webrtc/?token=..., handlers.ts:4735). 3) Optional explicit overrides for non-conventional hosts (the PR logs a warning telling you to use them): COGNIGY_ENDPOINT_BASE_URL, COGNIGY_WEBCHAT_BASE_URL, COGNIGY_STATIC_FILES_BASE_URL (config.ts:199-207). No new tool, operation, schema, or skill is added by this PR — it is config-layer only.
parityGaps: cognigy-vibe FAILS LOUDLY (raises ValueError) when the base URL isn't a recognizable CXone host; this plugin only logs a stderr warning (invisible in most MCP clients) and silently reuses the API URL as endpoint/webchat/static — the arsalan doc explicitly calls silence 'the worse failure mode', and this PR keeps it, just with a log line.

vibe hard-requires the literal 'cognigy-api-' prefix (CXone-only, strict); this plugin accepts any '(.*-)?api-' label — broader, but means typo'd hosts that happen to contain '-api-' derive plausible-looking wrong siblings instead of erroring.
No user-visible way to see the derived URLs before use (vibe's strictness surfaced misconfiguration at startup); here the first symptom would be a failing talk_to_agent call.

attacks.claim: Prior verdict 'merge with changes, rewrite description as tests+refactor' is directionally right but undersells the port fix and misses a fallback regression vs 31ac010's host-scoping.
attacks.reasoning: Verified both corrections. Port fix: real behavior change vs main (src/config.ts:71 drops explicit ports; PR preserves them with tests). Fallback regression: confirmed by tracing — main's fallback (config.ts:75-78) requires ^[a-z]+:// and is host-scoped, so scheme-less 'api-dev.cognigy.ai/notes-api-v2' returns unchanged; the PR's terminal `apiBaseUrl.replace(/\/(.*-)?api-/, '/$1endpoint-')` matches '/notes-api-' and rewrites the PATH to '/notes-endpoint-v2'. 31ac010's second commit message explicitly says it 'scopes the non-URL fallback to the host portion only', so the PR does undo a deliberate prior fix. It is actually worse than claimed: even a PARSEABLE URL with no api- hostname label (e.g. https://example.com/api-docs) falls through the warning into the same replace and becomes https://example.com/endpoint-docs — contradicting both the warning text ('Using the API URL unchanged') and the PR's own 'no api- label' test comment (that test host trial.nicecxone.com just happens to contain no 'api-' anywhere).

attacks.claim: Port-preservation is a real live fix the prior review missed: main drops an explicit port in derived URLs; PR #1 fixes and tests this, so the PR is not fully redundant.
attacks.reasoning: Confirmed. main src/config.ts:71 returns `${url.protocol}//${url.hostname}`; WHATWG URL.hostname never includes the port, so https://api-trial.cognigy.ai:8443 derives to https://endpoint-trial.cognigy.ai (port silently lost) for endpoint/webchat/static. The PR's deriveSiblingBaseUrl appends `url.port ? ":"+url.port : ""` and the diff adds exactly three port-preservation tests (.cognigy.ai endpoint, .cognigy.ai webchat+static, CXone :9443). The PR is therefore not fully redundant.

attacks.claim: The PR's rewritten parse-failure fallback `apiBaseUrl.replace(/\/(.*-)?api-/, ...)` is no longer host-scoped, reintroducing the path-rewrite hazard 31ac010 deliberately removed; should be restored to a host-scoped replace.
attacks.reasoning: Confirmed and understated. The diff replaces the host-scoped fallback (scheme/host/rest split with replace applied only to host) with a whole-string replace. Traced failure: 'api-dev.cognigy.ai/notes-api-v2' → path rewritten to 'notes-endpoint-v2' (main: unchanged). Additionally the replace is the terminal return for the warning path too, so parseable URLs whose PATH contains a hyphen-preceded or slash-preceded 'api-' get mangled even when the URL parsed fine — e.g. https://example.com/api-docs → https://example.com/endpoint-docs — despite the warning claiming the URL is used unchanged. 31ac010's second commit message ('scopes the non-URL fallback to the host portion only, so a path/query containing "api-" is never rewritten') proves this exact hazard was deliberately fixed before. Restoring the host-scoped replace is the right ask.

attacks.claim: The no-'api-'-label warning uses console.error (safe stderr for stdio MCP) but fires three times per boot for the same host; cosmetic only.
attacks.reasoning: Mostly confirmed: the diff uses console.error (stderr — safe for a stdio MCP server, matching existing practice), and loadConfig (config.ts:198-208) independently calls deriveEndpointBaseUrl, deriveWebchatBaseUrl and deriveStaticFilesBaseUrl when the COGNIGY_*_BASE_URL overrides are absent, so a no-api-label host logs three near-identical warnings per boot. One refutation of 'cosmetic only': the warning's text is misleading — it promises 'Using the API URL unchanged', but control then falls to the un-scoped replace, which CAN alter the URL when 'api-' appears in the path (see previous claim). The triple-fire itself is cosmetic; the message content is not purely cosmetic because it can be false.

usageCorrections: Step 1 setup command is not executable as written: `npx @cognigy/plugin-engine@latest cognigy-setup` cannot resolve — the package ships two bins (cognigy-setup, cognigy-mcp), neither named after the package, so npx has no default executable and would error ('could not determine executable to run'). README.md (lines 66/91/106) consistently documents the required form: `npx -y -p @cognigy/plugin-engine@latest cognigy-setup`. The interactive base-URL/API-key prompts themselves are real (src/setup.ts:181-195, 1001).

Minor line-ref drift: create_ai_agent builds endpointUrl at src/tools/handlers.ts:1599 (guide says 1600), and the webrtc link is built in buildWebrtcDemoUrl at handlers.ts:4733-4736 (guide's 4735 is inside it — fine). handleTalkToAgent:2068, webchat URL:4249, and overrides at config.ts:199-207 are all exact.

All tool names/params check out: talk_to_agent (message required; aiAgentId or endpointUrl optional), create_ai_agent (required: name), manage_webchat, manage_voice_gateway, audit_voice_agent all exist in src/tools/definitions.ts. The claim that the PR adds no tool/operation/schema/skill is correct — the diff touches only src/config.ts and src/__tests__/config.test.ts.

One caveat on step 3: the warning does tell you to set the COGNIGY_*_BASE_URL overrides, but for a non-conventional host whose PATH contains 'api-' the PR does not actually 'use the API URL unchanged' as the warning claims — the un-scoped fallback replace may rewrite the path (see findings). The overrides still work as documented (config.ts:199-207 short-circuits derivation).

title: feat(api): autodetect corporate CA trust store for TLS-inspecting proxies

findings.claim: macOS keychain export targets /System/Library/Keychains/SystemRootCertificates.keychain, but corporate/MDM CAs (NICE/Fortinet) live in /Library/Keychains/System.keychain, making the macOS branch a near-no-op for the corporate use case
findings.evidence: Diff (src/api/caBundle.ts, defaultCaBundleDeps.execFindCertificate) passes ["find-certificate","-a","-p","/System/Library/Keychains/SystemRootCertificates.keychain"]. Live check on this machine: `security find-certificate -a -c Nice /System/Library/Keychains/SystemRootCertificates.keychain` returns nothing (keychain holds 158 Apple public roots), while the same query against /Library/Keychains/System.keychain returns 'Nice Systems RootCA', 'NICE Issuing CA01', 'NICE-MDJ4RRK9PV'. Exporting Apple roots and merging with tls.rootCertificates adds zero corporate trust. The module's own doc comment even says 'export the login+System keychain roots' — the code does not do what the comment claims.

findings.claim: Tests mock execFindCertificate so the real keychain path is never exercised
findings.evidence: src/__tests__/caBundle.test.ts makeDeps() defaults execFindCertificate to () => undefined and every darwin test injects a fake (e.g. execFindCertificate: () => bundle). No test invokes defaultCaBundleDeps.execFindCertificate, so the wrong-keychain bug is invisible to the suite (all 420 tests pass).

findings.claim: Well-architected otherwise: pure resolveCaBundle(deps), zero new deps, wired via https.Agent({ca}), ca:undefined preserves behaviour
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED mechanics: resolveCaBundle takes injected deps (env/readFile/exists/platform/exec); diff touches only src/api/caBundle.ts, src/api/client.ts and two test files — no package.json change; client.ts adds `httpsAgent: new https.Agent({ ca })`; https.Agent({ca: undefined}) is Node-default behaviour, verified by client.test.ts. HOWEVER the architecture is not fully sound: (a) env/probe paths REPLACE the trust store (`ca: certs`) instead of augmenting it — Node's native NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS semantics are additive, so a user whose file contains only the corporate CA loses all public-CA trust and fails off-VPN with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE (only the macos-keychain branch merges tls.rootCertificates); (b) see new finding below — the macOS branch is dead code anyway.

findings.claim: Prior verdict: needs rework (fix keychain path)
findings.evidence: Verdict stands and is understated — beyond the wrong keychain, the macOS branch is unreachable dead code on real Macs (see newFindings), so the PR does not achieve its stated goal ('truststore equivalent', arsalan-diff-comparison.md item 9, 'enterprise blocker') for the team's actual platform (macOS + NICE SSL inspection) without env vars already set.

newFindings: DEAD CODE / ORDERING BUG: SYSTEM_BUNDLE_PATHS includes /etc/ssl/cert.pem (labelled 'Alpine'), but that file exists on every macOS install (verified locally: 333KB, 128 certs, 0 NICE certs — it is the LibreSSL copy of Apple public roots). Since the system-bundle probe runs BEFORE the darwin keychain branch in resolveCaBundle, on any real Mac with no env vars the function returns source=probe:system-bundle with Apple-roots-only and the macos-keychain code never executes. Combined with the replace-not-augment semantics, autodetection on macOS actively swaps Node's trust store for a corporate-CA-free bundle — worst case slightly narrowing trust, best case a no-op for the proxy problem. The darwin branch must run before (or the probe list must be platform-gated).

TRUST-STORE REPLACEMENT SEMANTICS: for env-var and probe sources the resolved certs are passed as https.Agent({ca: certs}) which REPLACES Node's default roots. Node's own NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS is additive. A user pointing NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS at a corp-CA-only PEM (common) would break all connections to publicly-signed endpoints when off the inspecting proxy. Should merge with tls.rootCertificates on every path, as the keychain branch already does.

SECURITY (minor): the combined-bundle probe auto-trusts a fixed world-writable-directory path /tmp/combined-ca.pem for ALL users of the plugin. Any local user/process can pre-create that file with a rogue CA and the MCP server will silently trust it (source only surfaces at LOG_LEVEL=debug). The shell-profile pattern it mimics is per-user opt-in; baking it into a published npm package is broader exposure. At minimum check ownership/permissions or make it opt-in.

Doc-comment vs code mismatch in caBundle.ts: header says step 3 exports 'the login+System keychain roots'; the code queries only SystemRootCertificates.keychain. PR body makes the same false claim ('merges the exported roots... so corporate... work out of the box').

usage.vibeExperience: In cognigy-vibe the Python package depends on `truststore` (arsalan-diff-comparison.md line 38 and item 9): at import time it injects the OS trust store into ssl, so on a corporate laptop behind NICE/Fortinet SSL inspection every httpx call to the Cognigy API just works — no env vars, no setup step, nothing visible to the user. The doc calls Node's lack of this 'an enterprise blocker for us'. Recommended action line 184: 'Add a truststore equivalent (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS / win-ca autodetection) for corporate proxies.'
usage.howToUseHere: This PR adds no MCP tool, operation, or skill — it is transparent transport plumbing inside CognigyApiClient. To exercise it in a live Claude Code session: (1) check out the PR branch and run `npm run plugin:dev` so the engine runs from src/ via tsx; (2) to test pure autodetection, launch Claude Code with the corporate env vars unset (`env -u NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS -u SSL_CERT_FILE -u REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE claude`) while on the NICE VPN; (3) set `LOG_LEVEL=debug` in the MCP server env and call any Cognigy tool (e.g. `manage_ai_agents { operation: "list" }`) — stderr shows `CA trust: using <source> (<path>)` telling you which of the 7 sources won (env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS → env:SSL_CERT_FILE → env:REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE → probe:combined-bundle (/tmp/combined-ca.pem) → probe:system-bundle → macos-keychain → node-default); (4) escape hatch identical to today: `export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/tmp/combined-ca.pem` before launching the client always wins. Note: on this team's standard setup (shell profile generates /tmp/combined-ca.pem and sets the env vars) the env-var path fires and works; the value-add is only for users WITHOUT that shell profile.
parityGaps: truststore delegates verification to the OS API per-connection (handles System.keychain corporate CAs, intermediates, revocation); this PR exports a static PEM once per process — and on macOS the export reads the wrong keychain AND is dead code behind the /etc/ssl/cert.pem probe, so a bare Mac behind NICE inspection still fails TLS, which was the entire point of the item
No Windows trust-store support at all (acknowledged in PR body; the migration doc explicitly asked for 'win-ca autodetection')
truststore augments existing trust; this PR's env/probe paths replace Node's roots, a regression vs both truststore and Node's native NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS semantics
truststore picks up keychain changes on new connections; this PR caches the bundle for the process lifetime (acceptable for a short-lived MCP server, but a difference)

validated.verdictRationale: The prior review's core bug is confirmed and there is a second, worse defect it missed: on macOS the keychain branch is unreachable because /etc/ssl/cert.pem (present on every Mac, Apple public roots only) satisfies the system-bundle probe first — so for the team's actual platform (macOS + NICE SSL inspection, the 'enterprise blocker' this PR exists to fix) autodetection resolves to a bundle with zero corporate CAs while also replacing Node's default trust store. Add to that the replace-vs-augment semantics regression on the env-var paths and the /tmp/combined-ca.pem auto-trust exposure. The structure (pure resolveCaBundle(deps), zero deps, good tests of the dispatch logic) is worth keeping, but the fix set is: query System.keychain (and login) or use `security find-certificate -a -p` with no keychain arg / `security export`, run the darwin branch before (or gate /etc/ssl/cert.pem out of) the probe list, merge every source with tls.rootCertificates, and reconsider the /tmp probe. Until then the PR only genuinely helps Linux users and users who already set the env vars — who were already fine.

attacks.claim: macOS keychain export targets SystemRootCertificates.keychain while corporate CAs live in /Library/Keychains/System.keychain, making the macOS branch a near-no-op for the corporate use case
attacks.reasoning: Verified in the diff: defaultCaBundleDeps.execFindCertificate runs `security find-certificate -a -p /System/Library/Keychains/SystemRootCertificates.keychain`. Re-ran the live checks myself: `security find-certificate -a -c NICE -p /System/Library/Keychains/SystemRootCertificates.keychain` returns nothing (that keychain holds 158 Apple public roots), while the same query against /Library/Keychains/System.keychain returns 'Nice Systems RootCA', 'NICE Issuing CA01', 'NICE-MDJ4RRK9PV'. Exporting Apple roots and merging with tls.rootCertificates adds zero corporate trust. The module doc comment (step 3) indeed says 'export the login+System keychain roots' — the code does not query either of those keychains.

attacks.claim: Tests mock execFindCertificate so the real keychain path is never exercised
attacks.reasoning: Confirmed from the diff of src/__tests__/caBundle.test.ts: makeDeps() defaults execFindCertificate to `() => undefined`, and every darwin test injects a fake (`execFindCertificate: () => bundle` or garbage). defaultCaBundleDeps is never imported or invoked by any test, so the wrong-keychain choice is invisible to the suite. Minor caveat: the '420 tests pass' figure comes from the PR body — no CI checks are reported on the feat/tls-trust-store branch, so the count is unverified, but the substantive claim (real keychain path untested) is directly confirmed by the test code.

attacks.claim: PARTIAL: architecture is clean (pure resolveCaBundle(deps), zero new deps, https.Agent({ca}) wiring, ca:undefined preserves defaults) BUT env/probe paths replace rather than augment the trust store
attacks.reasoning: All mechanics confirmed: diff touches exactly 4 files (caBundle.ts, client.ts, two new test files), no package.json change; resolveCaBundle takes injected env/readFile/exists/platform/execFindCertificate; client.ts adds `httpsAgent: new https.Agent({ ca })`; client.test.ts verifies ca:undefined leaves the agent's ca unset (Node default). The replace-not-augment criticism is also correct: the env and both probe branches return `{ ca: certs, source }` without merging tls.rootCertificates — only the macos-keychain branch merges (`[...tls.rootCertificates, ...certs]`). Node's https.Agent `ca` option overrides the default root store, whereas native NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS is additive, so a corp-CA-only PEM would break publicly-signed endpoints off-VPN.

attacks.claim: Prior verdict 'needs rework (fix keychain path)' stands and is understated
attacks.reasoning: Given claims 1 and 5 (both confirmed), on the team's actual platform (macOS + NICE SSL inspection) with no env vars set, the PR never adds the corporate CA: the darwin branch is unreachable (system-bundle probe wins first) and even if reached it queries the wrong keychain. The PR body's headline ('works out of the box... enterprise blocker', arsalan item #9) is not achieved. Rework needed on at least: keychain target, branch ordering/platform gating, and augment-vs-replace semantics.

attacks.claim: NEW: dead code / ordering bug — /etc/ssl/cert.pem exists on macOS, the system-bundle probe runs before the darwin branch, so the macOS keychain code never executes on a real Mac
attacks.reasoning: Confirmed both halves. Code order in resolveCaBundle is env → COMBINED_BUNDLE_PATHS → SYSTEM_BUNDLE_PATHS → `if (deps.platform === 'darwin')`. SYSTEM_BUNDLE_PATHS includes '/etc/ssl/cert.pem' (commented 'Alpine'). Verified locally: /etc/ssl/cert.pem exists on this Mac (333,483 bytes, 128 PEM certs, 0 matches for NICE/Fortinet — the LibreSSL copy of Apple roots). So with no env vars the function returns probe:system-bundle (or probe:combined-bundle if /tmp/combined-ca.pem exists, as on team machines) and the keychain branch is unreachable. One precision nit: on team Macs the shell profile leaves /tmp/combined-ca.pem behind, so the winning source there is probe:combined-bundle, not probe:system-bundle — but that doesn't rescue the darwin branch, which is dead either way. Combined with replace semantics, macOS autodetection swaps Node's roots for a corp-CA-free Apple-roots bundle.

attacks.claim: NEW: trust-store replacement semantics — https.Agent({ca}) replaces Node defaults for env/probe sources; should merge with tls.rootCertificates like the keychain branch does
attacks.reasoning: Confirmed in the diff: env branch returns `{ ca: certs, source }`, combined-bundle and system-bundle branches likewise — no tls.rootCertificates merge; only macos-keychain merges. Node's tls docs: the `ca` option replaces the trusted CA set; NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS native behaviour extends it. Failure scenario is real: user with NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS pointing at a corp-root-only PEM gets UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE / self-signed errors against publicly-signed endpoints when off the inspecting proxy — a behaviour regression vs native Node handling of the same env var.

attacks.claim: NEW: security (minor) — auto-trusting the fixed world-writable path /tmp/combined-ca.pem with no ownership/permission check
attacks.reasoning: Confirmed: COMBINED_BUNDLE_PATHS = ['/tmp/combined-ca.pem']; the probe does exists() + readFile() + PEM-split with no owner/mode check. /tmp (→ /private/tmp) is world-writable (sticky bit prevents deletion by others but not pre-creation of an absent file by any local user). The chosen source is surfaced only via logger.debug, and the repo's logger defaults to 'info' (src/config.ts LOG_LEVEL default 'info'), so silent by default. The per-user shell-profile pattern this mimics is opt-in; a published npm package probing it for all users is broader exposure. Severity 'minor' is fair — requires a local attacker — but the finding is accurate.

attacks.claim: NEW: doc-comment vs code mismatch ('login+System keychain roots' vs SystemRootCertificates.keychain) and matching false PR-body claim
attacks.reasoning: Doc-comment mismatch confirmed verbatim: caBundle.ts header step 3 says 'best-effort export the login+System keychain roots via `security find-certificate -a -p`', while the code passes only /System/Library/Keychains/SystemRootCertificates.keychain. usage.howToUseHere: All commands run from any shell, no env vars needed (credentials are read from ~/.cognigy-plugin/config.json, written 0600 by the original install wizard). 1) Check install health: `npx -y @cognigy/plugin-engine@latest cognigy-setup status` — prints per-surface versions plus either 'No drift detected.' or a 'Drift detected (n):' list (Claude Code plugin version vs npm latest via `claude plugin list --json`; Desktop connector entry in claude_desktop_config.json; Desktop launcher file ~/.cognigy-plugin/desktop-launch.mjs; Desktop engine version under ~/.cognigy-plugin/engine) with the exact fix each needs. 2) Self-heal: `npx -y @cognigy/plugin-engine@latest cognigy-setup status --fix` — applies each fix independently: stale Claude Code plugin → `claude plugin update cognigy@cognigy-plugin`; missing launcher → rewrites desktop-launch.mjs; stale/missing Desktop engine → `npm install @cognigy/plugin-engine@<latest> --prefix ~/.cognigy-plugin/engine`; missing Desktop connector entry → rebuilt from stored creds file, or if no COGNIGY_API_KEY is stored it prints 're-run cognigy-setup install --client claude-desktop'. One failed fix does not stop the others. 3) Dry-run update check: `npx -y @cognigy/plugin-engine@latest cognigy-setup update --check` — prints 'Claude Code plugin: update available (1.6.0 → 1.7.0)' / 'Claude Desktop engine: update available (… applies automatically on next Desktop restart)' or 'Everything is up to date.' without changing anything; plain `cognigy-setup update` still applies. 4) Remove: `npx -y @cognigy/plugin-engine@latest cognigy-setup uninstall` (TTY confirmation; `--yes`/`-y` for non-interactive, exits 1 without it on non-TTY; `--purge` also deletes the shared ~/.cognigy-plugin dir; `--client claude-code|claude-desktop|...` to scope). No MCP tool calls or skills are involved — this is purely the cognigy-setup CLI surface.
parityGaps: Drift detection/--check only covers Claude Code + Claude Desktop; Antigravity, Codex, and Gemini installs (which this repo's installer also manages) get no reconciliation, so 'No drift detected' / 'Everything is up to date' can be false for those surfaces — vibe's reconcile.py covered all of its surfaces (package version, marketplace pin, plugin version, Desktop pin).
No Windows cognigy-setup.ps1 equivalent (arsalan item #6 names it explicitly); the Node CLI works on Windows but there is no PowerShell entry point.
No marketplace-pin drift check (vibe's reconcile diffs the marketplace pin; here the marketplace add is assumed idempotent and never verified).
Plain colored console output rather than vibe's 'rich TUI' (cosmetic).
uninstall gained no new capability in this PR (it pre-existed) — parity there was already met, just now tested.

findings.claim: Staleness gap: resolveFlowForAgent strategy-3 keys on '{agent.name} Flow'; agent rename doesn't invalidate the old flow name-mapping — real untested staleness path, low blast radius (fallback strategy only)
findings.evidence: handlers.ts diff: strategy 3 does `const flowName = `${agent.name} Flow`; const cachedByName = cacheStore?.resolveId("flow", flowName)`. handleUpdateAiAgent's agent patch calls only `this.cacheStore?.invalidate("agent", aiAgentId)` — no forgetId/forgetIdByValue on the "flow" (or "agent") name namespaces. No test covers rename → mapping staleness. newFindings: Name→id map has NO TTL and persists across process restarts indefinitely (ProjectState .state.json on disk): unlike the 5-min read cache, a stale name→id mapping made during active use is only ever cleared by a >4h idle gap or an in-process delete. Out-of-band changes (teammate renames/deletes a flow in the Cognigy UI) during an active session are masked without bound — the read cache self-heals in 5 min, the name map never does. This is the general form of the rename gap and worth a doc note or a per-mapping TTL.

Multi-process name-map clobbering: two concurrently-running MCP servers against the same base URL share <state>/.state.json; ProjectState keeps state in memory and save() rewrites the whole file, so process B's later save() can resurrect a mapping process A just forgot (forgetIdByValue undone). Read-cache files are per-entry so they are cross-process coherent; only the state file has last-writer-wins semantics. Low severity, opt-in feature, but unhandled.

Correctness is fine — arguably better error surfacing — but it is an undocumented extra API call per code-node update.

usage.vibeExperience: cognigy-vibe's push_code_node / push_agent_tool / push_html_node (ben-diff-notes.md item 1, arsalan item #2): instead of regenerating an entire code-node script, tool-parameters JSON Schema, or xApp HTML blob as an inline tool parameter on every incremental edit (the team's biggest observed token waste), the agent maintains the artifact as a local file using native Write/Edit + local linting/LSP, and tells the MCP a file path to push. Vibe additionally diff-checks the remote before pushing to block clobbering concurrent human/agent edits.
usage.howToUseHere:
Prereq: plugin installed for Claude Code with creds wired (one-time: `npx @cognigy/plugin-engine@latest cognigy-setup`, or env COGNIGY_API_BASE_URL + COGNIGY_API_KEY). The engine must run locally over stdio (the default npx launch) — filePath fails by design on a remote/Desktop-connector deployment.

1. Code node, create-from-file: write the script locally (e.g. Write /Users/you/proj/flow/compute.js), then call MCP tool `manage_flow_nodes` { operation: "create", flowId, parentNodeId: <toolNodeId>, mode: "appendChild", nodeType: "code", label: "Compute", filePath: "/Users/you/proj/flow/compute.js" } — the server reads the file and pushes it as config.code. Provide filePath OR config.code, never both.
2. Code node, iterate: Edit the local file, then `manage_flow_nodes` { operation: "update", flowId, nodeId, filePath: "/Users/you/proj/flow/compute.js" }. After the push the handler reads the node back and surfaces a `_hints.warning` if the code failed to transpile (hasError) — fix locally and re-push.
3. xApp HTML node: same filePath param with nodeType "showXAppHtml" on create, or on update of an existing setHTMLAppState node — pushes to config.html.
4. Agent tool parameter schemas: keep the JSON Schema at e.g. /Users/you/proj/tools/search-params.json and call `create_tool` { aiAgentId, toolType: "tool", name, config: { toolId, description }, parametersFilePath: "/Users/you/proj/tools/search-params.json" } or `update_tool` { aiAgentId, toolNodeId, toolType: "tool", parametersFilePath: ... }. The server parses the file and rejects invalid JSON or a non-object (array/scalar/null) before any API write; useParameters is set automatically.
5. Path rules: paths must be absolute; ENOENT returns 'File not found: <path>', other read failures return 'Failed to read <path>: <os message>', all before any POST/PATCH.
6. Discoverability: the flow-nodes and tools-setup skills (auto-loaded on intent in Claude Code) now document the pattern, so the model picks it up without prompting; you can also just say 'maintain this code node as a local file and push it'.
parityGaps: No conflict/diff detection: vibe blocks a push when the remote content changed since the local copy was taken (human or other agent wrote in between); this PR pushes unconditionally — clobber protection is deferred to migration item #6 on a separate branch.

Push-only: no tool to pull/seed a local file from an existing node's remote content (vibe's workflow assumes a maintained local copy); here you must manage_flow_nodes get and write config.code/html to disk yourself.

Coverage is three targets (code → config.code, setHTMLAppState → config.html, aiAgentJobTool parameters) — matches vibe's three push_* tools, but any other large config field still requires inline content.

Local-only by design: on a remote/server-hosted MCP (e.g. Claude Desktop's wired connector) filePath always fails with a read error; vibe had the same constraint but the doc note in ben-diff-notes.md about reimplementing write/edit for remote deployments is not addressed.
Documented extension requirements (.js/.ts/.html/.json) are not actually enforced — cosmetic doc/code mismatch.

validated.verdictRationale: The prior review holds up under re-validation with only cosmetic corrections (4 call sites not 3; only ENOENT gets a truly distinct message). The implementation is well-scoped and defensive: pure injectable helper, absolute-path and exactly-one-of enforcement at both helper and handler level, JSON content validation before any API write, every failure path proven to skip POST/PATCH, inline behavior byte-identical for existing callers, and the aiAgentJob preview gotcha deliberately avoided. The confirmed doc/code mismatch (unenforced extension claims in definitions.ts and SKILL.md) and the incidental extra read-back GET on code-node updates are both harmless and can land as a trivial follow-up; neither justifies blocking. The known parity gaps vs cognigy-vibe (conflict detection, pull direction) are explicitly and correctly deferred to migration item #6 rather than being omissions of this PR.
